name: AMA - Association of Friends of the Autistic (São Paulo)
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista (AMA)
summary: Founded in São Paulo in 1983 by parents of autistic children, the first autism association in Brazil and Latin America. Runs education, therapy and social-assistance programmes and maintains a national directory of partner autism institutions.
notes: Won the UNESCO Human Rights Prize in 1998. Anchor organisation of a nationwide network of independently run AMA-branded associations in other cities and states, several catalogued separately in this file.

name: AMA Alagoas
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Alagoas
summary: Parent-founded autism association in Maceió, part of the national AMA network, providing therapy, education and family support for autistic children and adults in Alagoas state.
notes: Listed as AMA-AL in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMA Florianópolis
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Florianópolis
summary: Santa Catarina autism association affiliated with the national AMA network, providing education, therapeutic support and family guidance for autistic people in Florianópolis.
notes: Listed as AMA-SC Florianópolis in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMAS - Friends of Autistic People of Sorocaba
name_local: Associação Amigos dos Autistas de Sorocaba (AMAS)
summary: Nonprofit founded in Sorocaba, São Paulo state, in 1994 for the diagnosis, treatment and habilitation of autistic children aged 2 to 12, with health, education and social-assistance services and family support.
notes: Part of the AMA-affiliated network of family-founded autism associations across Brazil, independently incorporated in Sorocaba.

name: AMA Ribeirão Preto
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Ribeirão Preto
summary: Family-founded autism association in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, offering education, therapeutic care and support groups for autistic people and their relatives.
notes: Independent AMA-network affiliate, distinct from the USP Ribeirão Preto Hearing Voices Network already catalogued in this city.

name: AMA Campo Grande
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Campo Grande
summary: Mato Grosso do Sul autism association in the national AMA network, providing therapy, special education and family support services in Campo Grande.
region: Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
notes: Listed as AMA-MS in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMAI - Friends of Autistic People of Itu
name_local: AMAI - Associação Amigos dos Autistas de Itu
summary: Family-founded association in Itu, São Paulo state, providing therapeutic, educational and social-assistance support to autistic children, youth and adults.
notes: Part of the wider network of AMA-branded family associations in São Paulo state municipalities.

name: AMA Joinville
name_local: Associação dos Amigos do Autista de Joinville
summary: Santa Catarina autism association serving Joinville and the surrounding region with therapeutic, educational and family-support services, part of the national AMA network.

name: AMA Itajaí
summary: Autism association in Itajaí, Santa Catarina, describing its mission as building a society where autistic people 'have a place and a voice,' offering therapeutic and educational support.

name: AAMPARA (AMA Curitiba)
name_local: Associação de Atendimento e Apoio ao Autista do Brasil (AAMPARA), trade name AMA - Amigos Pelo Autista
summary: Curitiba nonprofit founded in 2006 to improve the quality of life of autistic children and adolescents, operating under the trade name AMA within the national AMA network.

name: AUMA - Friends of the Autistic Child Association
name_local: AUMA - Associação dos Amigos da Criança Autista
summary: São Paulo association providing clinical, psychoeducational and psychomotor support for autistic children and adults, staffed by social workers, psychomotor therapists and pedagogical specialists.
notes: Distinct from same-acronym AMA-network entities in other states; based in São Paulo city, not to be confused with any Rio Grande do Sul organisation of a similar name.

name: Casa da Esperança Foundation
name_local: Fundação Casa da Esperança
summary: Fortaleza-based foundation providing autism diagnosis, education and family-training services, an early producer of Brazilian podcasts on autism and a long-running reference institution in Ceará.
notes: Site only resolves over plain HTTP, not HTTPS, in verification checks; distinct from ABRAÇA, also based in Fortaleza.

name: Museum of Images of the Unconscious
name_local: Museu de Imagens do Inconsciente
summary: Rio de Janeiro museum founded in 1952 by psychiatrist Nise da Silveira within a former psychiatric hospital in Engenho de Dentro, housing roughly 350,000 artworks made by psychiatric patients through occupational art therapy.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Collection registered as Brazilian national heritage by IPHAN; part of the Instituto Municipal Nise da Silveira, whose grounds also host the Loucura Suburbana carnival bloc catalogued separately.

name: ASTOC - Solidarity Association for OCD and Tourette Syndrome
name_local: Astoc ST - Associação Solidária do TOC e Síndrome de Tourette
summary: São Paulo association founded in 1996 to spread information on OCD and Tourette syndrome, fund research and support patient socialisation, running peer support groups with trained facilitators and partner groups in other states.
notes: Partners with RIOSTOC (Rio de Janeiro, already catalogued) and with hospital-based OCD programme PROTOC, also catalogued in this file.

name: Instituto Lagarta Vira Pupa
summary: Online support network for families of disabled and autistic people, grown from a 2012 blog by journalist Andréa Werner after her son's autism diagnosis into an institute in 2021 with around 300 volunteer ambassadors nationwide.
notes: Parent-led rather than autistic-led. No single fixed office confirmed; site content references São Paulo, Bauru and Campinas, so the São Paulo coordinate is an approximation for a nationwide online network.

name: Suburban Madness Carnival Bloc
name_local: Bloco Carnavalesco Loucura Suburbana
summary: Rio de Janeiro carnival bloc and cultural centre created in 2001 at the Instituto Municipal Nise da Silveira, bringing mental-health service users, family members, staff and neighbours together for street carnival and, since 2010, year-round workshops in samba, music and costume-making.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Rio's first mental-health Ponto de Cultura (Culture Point), 2010. Located on the same grounds as the Museum of Images of the Unconscious, catalogued separately.

name: Autistic Collective of UFPB
name_local: Coletivo Autista da UFPB (CAU)
summary: Student-run collective at the Federal University of Paraíba in João Pessoa supporting autistic students, seeking volunteer professionals to assist members and running accessibility workshops such as AI-for-accessibility sessions.
notes: Part of the wave of autistic student collectives that followed USP's CAUSP (already catalogued) from 2021 onward.

name: Stim Collective (UFPR)
name_local: Coletivo Stim - UFPR
summary: Autistic student collective at the Federal University of Paraná in Curitiba, launched as a university extension project to build representation and peer support for autistic students on campus.
notes: No independent website found; UFPR's accessibility coordination (CAS) separately reports serving 677 autistic students as of the source article.

name: UnB Autism and Neurodiversity Nucleus
name_local: Núcleo de Autismo e Neurodiversidade da UnB
summary: Support nucleus at the University of Brasília created jointly by autistic and neurodivergent students and psychology staff, offering psychological care, guidance for professors and an annual Autism Visibility Week.
notes: Source article quotes autistic and neurodivergent students describing the nucleus as their own initiative, run jointly with psychology-service staff; linked to UnB's Center for Psychological Care and Studies (Caep).

name: Campinas Hearing Voices Group (CEI)
name_local: CEI Campinas - Grupo de Ouvidores de Vozes
summary: Peer support group for voice-hearers run by the Centro de Estudos e Pesquisas em Reabilitação (CEI) in Campinas, part of the Brazilian offshoot of the international Hearing Voices Movement.
notes: Sister initiative to the USP Ribeirão Preto Hearing Voices Network already catalogued in this dataset; part of a wider set of Brazilian Ouvidores de Vozes groups that also met in Curitiba, Belo Horizonte and Porto Alegre without independent websites found.

name: Brazilian Federation of Down Syndrome Associations
name_local: Federação Brasileira das Associações de Síndrome de Down (FBASD)
summary: Brasília-based federation, founded in 1994, uniting more than 50 Down syndrome associations across Brazil's five regions; created a National Group of Self-Advocates in 2016 that trains young people and adults with Down syndrome as self-advocates and mediators.
notes: Federation itself is run by member associations and professionals, but explicitly sponsors a national self-advocates group of people with Down syndrome.

name: National Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação Nacional das APAEs (APAE Brasil)
summary: Brasília-based umbrella federation of more than 2,000 local APAE associations serving people with intellectual and multiple disabilities across Brazil, operating for over 60 years and running a national self-advocates programme (Encontro Nacional de Autodefensores).
notes: Historically family- and professional-led, but its self-advocacy programme has produced autodefensores who represent users on bodies such as the National Social Assistance Council. Several state federations (FEAPAES) are catalogued separately in this file.

name: Autism and Reality
name_local: Autismo e Realidade
summary: São Paulo organisation founded in 2010 by parents after their daughter's autism diagnosis, publishing guidance booklets and research since 2015 under the José Luiz Egydio Setúbal Foundation's PENSI Institute, combining a parents' council with a professional council.
notes: Also awards the A&R Prof. Dr. Marcos Tomanik Mercadante prize for autism research and training.

name: Canal Autismo / Revista Autismo
summary: Brazilian autism media outlet publishing Revista Autismo, launched in 2010 as the first Portuguese-language autism magazine, by the nonprofit Consciência Solidária based in Atibaia, São Paulo; distributes news, a free quarterly print edition and video content.
notes: Site blocks bare automated requests (403) but was confirmed live via search-engine indexing and third-party citation; described as the first magazine on autism in Latin America and the world.

name: APAE Três Pontas
summary: Local chapter of the APAE network in Três Pontas, Minas Gerais, serving about 4,000 people with intellectual and other disabilities through education, rehabilitation, supported employment and a dedicated Self-Management, Self-Advocacy and Family Program.
notes: Included as an example of a local APAE chapter with an explicit self-advocacy (autogestão/autodefesa) programme, distinct from the national and state federations catalogued separately.

name: PROTOC - Obsessive-Compulsive Spectrum Disorders Program
name_local: Programa Transtorno do Espectro Obsessivo-Compulsivo (PROTOC)
summary: Research, teaching and patient-care programme on the obsessive-compulsive spectrum run by the Psychiatry Institute of the University of São Paulo's Hospital das Clínicas, recruiting research volunteers and publishing patient-facing education.
notes: Hospital- and university-affiliated, not self-advocate led. Listed as a partner organisation by ASTOC, catalogued separately.

name: Autistic Collective of Vitória da Conquista
name_local: Coletivo Autista de Vitória da Conquista
summary: University collective formed in 2022 by autistic students from UESB, IFBA, UFBA and private colleges in Vitória da Conquista, Bahia, meeting biweekly to build visibility and mutual support around neurodivergence in higher education.
notes: No independent website found; verified via local news outlet. Multi-institution collective spanning one public state university, one federal institute and one federal university.

name: UFU Autism Spectrum Collective
name_local: Coletivo de estudantes com TEA da UFU
summary: Student collective at the Federal University of Uberlândia founded in April 2023, proposed by an autistic journalism student and supported by two professors, meeting regularly and communicating through Instagram.
notes: Proposed by autistic student Paulo Félix with staff backing from professors Valéria Asnis and Nuno Manna; no independent website, only Instagram.

name: AMAES - Friends of Autistic People of Espírito Santo
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista do Espírito Santo (AMAES)
summary: State-wide autism association founded in 2001 and headquartered in Vitória, with units across Espírito Santo, offering social assistance, specialised education, health and rehabilitation services and public-awareness campaigns.
notes: Operates additional units in Aracruz, Serra, Cariacica, Vila Velha and Viana.

name: UFPA Accessibility Coordination
name_local: Coordenadoria de Acessibilidade (Coacess) - UFPA
summary: Accessibility unit of the Federal University of Pará in Belém providing individualised pedagogical, psychological and occupational-therapy support to autistic and intellectually disabled students, alongside Libras and Braille services for other disabilities.
notes: Institutional support unit, not a student-run collective; reports serving 20 autistic and 8 intellectually disabled students as of the source article. No specific Indigenous or quilombola programme found despite searching.

name: APAE Aracaju
summary: Sergipe chapter of the APAE network, founded in 1970, serving around 600 people with intellectual and multiple disabilities across 33 municipalities and running an explicit self-advocacy (autodefensoria) programme.
notes: Site explicitly names an Autodefensoria strengthening self-advocates' protagonism, so marked mixed leadership rather than purely ally-led.

name: Pernambuco State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação Estadual das APAEs de Pernambuco (FEAPAES-PE)
summary: State federation coordinating APAE chapters across Pernambuco, headquartered in Caruaru, providing training and resource support to affiliated associations serving people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: Rio Grande do Norte State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte (FEAPAES-RN)
summary: Natal-based state federation coordinating APAE chapters across Rio Grande do Norte, providing educational programmes, social services and community-inclusion initiatives for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: Mato Grosso State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado de Mato Grosso (FEAPAES-MT)
summary: Cuiabá-based state federation linking local APAE associations across Mato Grosso, running training programmes and self-advocacy and self-management forums for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: Site describes forums for self-advocacy and self-management (autogestão), so marked mixed rather than purely ally-led. State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately.

name: Tocantins State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Tocantins (FEAPAES-TO)
summary: Palmas-based state federation coordinating APAE chapters across Tocantins, facilitating educational programmes, employment opportunities and cultural events for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: Acre State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Acre (FEAPAES-AC)
summary: Rio Branco-based state federation supporting local APAE chapters across Acre, including smaller-city affiliates such as Sena Madureira, and campaigning on disability rights.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: AMA Amazonas (Manaus)
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista do Amazonas
summary: Manaus autism association founded in 1997 by parents and friends of autistic people, the only organisation in the city serving autistic adults from age 14, offering social-assistance, health and education services.
notes: No independent working website found (only social media); existence and current activity confirmed via a Manaus municipal government news article about a service partnership.

name: Centro Conviver
summary: Curitiba clinical and educational centre founded in 1998 serving autistic adolescents, young adults and adults using the TEACCH model, working with families, schools, universities and employers on inclusion.
notes: One of the few Brazilian autism organisations focused specifically on adolescents and adults rather than young children.

name: APAE Belo Horizonte
summary: Belo Horizonte chapter of the APAE network, operating for more than 60 years, running a health clinic, an inclusive school, supported-employment programmes and residential care for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: No self-advocacy programme found stated on its site, unlike APAE Aracaju or APAE Três Pontas catalogued separately.

name: APAE Florianópolis
summary: Florianópolis chapter of the APAE network, providing services for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities in Santa Catarina's capital.
notes: Site content was minimal at verification time; included for state/city coverage as a working, live local APAE chapter distinct from the autism-specific AMA Florianópolis catalogued separately.
